acceptance: `go test -count=1 ./cmd/evolve` finishes well under its pre-fix 105-127s on the loop host, measured before and after, with the measurement recorded in the PR
A package wall-time budget check fails (red first) when a package's measured go-test wall time exceeds its budget, and names the package, its time and the budget
The budget is one named value, well below addedtests.PackageTimeout, so an honest runtime is caught long before any floor or ship deadline
fix: Profile ./cmd/evolve's suite (go test -json elapsed per test; the slow tests are its seam and loop tests) and cut its wall time: move whole-tree or loop-driving tests behind cheaper seams, parallelize independent tests, and split the package if its size is the cause. Then add a package wall-time budget check (for example a make target or a CI step over go test -json package elapsed times) with one named budget, so a package's honest runtime cannot creep up to a gate's deadline unnoticed again.
source: console, 2026-10-05, the build floor test-budget fix (fix/floor-test-budget-single-source) after cycles 1787/1791/1792/1798
summary: ./cmd/evolve's unit tests take 105-127s on the loop host and keep growing (46s at ADR-0083 in cycle 1270). The build floor killed the green package at a 120s literal deadline in cycles 1787, 1791, 1792 and 1798. The floor fix moves every floor go-test run onto addedtests.PackageTimeout (20m), which removes the false RED but also removes the 120s deadline that ADR-0083 had treated as the alarm for a slow ordinary package. Nothing now notices a package's honest runtime creeping toward a gate's deadline.
title: Cut ./cmd/evolve's unit-test wall time and add a package wall-time budget check
